page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The CPU includes 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1d cache. Memory resources consist of 32.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance has a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, contains no local NVMe storage, and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scores of 2211.0 and text processing scores of 2952.0 ranking in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression at 34.45 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.45 GB/sec both place in the top 25% tier. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the average middle 50% range, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 13253.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 29107.56. For small language model inference using a 135M model, the instance achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 348.03 tokens/sec, while medium model 7B text generation operates at an average speed of 16.4 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the c8i.4xlarge offers a compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2, making it a cost-efficient option for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. The absence of local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which represents a tradeoff for I/O-intensive database workloads. However, the inclusion of advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions provides hardware-accelerated execution for cryptography and matrix operations without requiring GPU resources.

This instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, single-threaded text processing, web serving, and small-to-medium scale machine learning inference. The high single-core performance and specialized instruction sets also make it appropriate for cryptographic tasks, data compression pipelines, and general-purpose application servers that require dedicated CPU allocation.
